oewn-01781131-v.learner: to find something enjoyable or pleasant.
examples: "I like her appearance," said Elizabeth, struck with other ideas.

oewn-01780873-v.learner: to be fond of someone or something.
examples: And so, you like this man's sisters, too, do you?

oewn-01828678-v.learner: to hope for, to want, or to prefer to have or to do something.
examples: "My love, should not you like to see a place of which you have heard so much?"

oewn-08659612-n.learner: a general area rather than one exact spot.
examples: They are gone down to Newcastle, a place quite northward it seems.

oewn-08682181-n.learner: a spot in an area, fixed by what is around it on the ground.
examples: We stopped at a shady place beside the river and ate our lunch.

oewn-08530790-n.learner: any area kept for a particular use.
examples: The possibility of meeting Mr. Darcy, while viewing the place, instantly occurred.

oewn-06495143-n.learner: one item on a list or in an order of things.
examples: But in the first place, he was like him.

oewn-00146749-r.learner: to the amount or the degree that is needed.
examples: "This walk is not wide enough for our party."
he is wise enough to assume even the appearance of what is right

oewn-15191509-n.learner: the last part of the day, when the light fades from late afternoon until dark.
examples: "This must be a most inconvenient sitting-room for the evening in summer: the windows are full west."

oewn-15192953-n.learner: the early part of the night, from dinner until bedtime, spent in some special way.

oewn-80042148-n.learner: a set phrase people say when they meet or leave someone, to wish them a good evening.
examples: "Good evening, ladies," he said, bowing as he came into the room.
I have just had a letter from Jane, with such dreadful news.
I am, therefore, by no means discouraged by what you have just said

oewn-00159432-r.learner: used to show that something is exact.
examples: it is just as he chooses.

oewn-00145758-r.learner: in a way that leaves no doubt.

oewn-00031700-r.learner: of an action or a state: going on as before, with no change, no break, and no stop.
examples: The park paling was still the boundary on one side.
He was always to have gone on Saturday, and to Saturday he still meant to stay.

oewn-00018101-r.learner: to an even greater degree, used with words that compare.
examples: Their situation was awkward enough; but hers she thought was still worse.

oewn-00027761-r.learner: all the same, in spite of anything that points the other way.
examples: It rained hard all morning; still, we set out for the village.

oewn-02008888-v.learner: to go or come back to a place, a condition, or an activity you were in before.

She stood several minutes before the picture, and returned to it again before they quitted the gallery.

oewn-00818014-v.learner: to say something back in answer.

oewn-04627573-n.learner: the mix of qualities in a person that decides how they act and how they judge right and wrong.

oewn-09610740-n.learner: a made-up person in a story, a play, or a film.

oewn-14462159-n.learner: a good name among other people.
